frontier.hypothesis: Directed permuter over PERM_STMT_LIST reorderings + PERM_ADD_SUB / PERM_DUMMY_COMMA_EXPR / PERM_REORDER_DECLS mutations finds a spelling that shifts sll's LUID above move16's WITHOUT (a) introducing a second tree-level a0<<4 (s6's local/global pool split) OR (b) source-ordering i=a0 before v1=a0<<4 in a straight-line block (s7's cse.c operand substitution).

Permuter can explore C shapes routing around BOTH — e.g. mutations that split blocks so cse.c doesn't see i=a0 -> v1=a0<<4 in one processing region, or eliminate the second tree-level shift via non-obvious commutative/associative rewrites. s8 rederive confirms hand-derivation (including m2c-guided) has exhausted the axis.

frontier.hypothesis: A C spelling that expresses `v1 = a0<<4` and `i = a0` across a control-flow join (rather than a straight-line block) prevents cse.c's basic-block-scoped value-numbering from seeing them as value-equivalent, breaking the CSE fold that shortens a0's live range in the rotation branch.
frontier.mechanism: cse.c's basic_block_extended_end / cse_extended_basic_block bounds value-numbering to a single processing region. Cross-block equivalences are established only at reload/global. If i=a0 lives in one block and v1=a0<<4 in a different block reachable from function entry (not a linear predecessor of i=a0), CSE cannot substitute at insn 17. s8 note: no obvious semantically-purposeful early-guard exists (a0/a1 have no null/range semantics that would justify a natural if-guard), so this frontier likely requires either (a) a permuter find or (b) a novel semantic-invariant CFG rewrite not yet hand-derived.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate small C rewrites that split the prologue into two joinable blocks with semantic purpose — e.g. a bounds check on a0 vs D_800A33AC before v1 compute (if a0>=count, skip both loops but still update D_800A33A0/A4); or a conditional-move idiom that GCC lowers to a jump. Verify each keeps score close and doesn't add insns. Measure whether cse.c picks up value-equivalence across the split.
